        some i
    resource := input.resource_changes[i]
    resource.type == "aws_iam_role"

}

is_valid_iam_role_policy_attachment {
                 some i
    resource := input.configuration.root_module.resources[i]
    resource.type == "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment"
    resource.expressions.role.references[0] == "aws_iam_role.eb_ec2_role.name"
    resource.expressions.policy_arn.constant_value == "arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AWSElasticBeanstalkWebTier"
}

                 some i

    resource.type == "aws_iam_instance_profile"
    resource.expressions.role.references[0] == "aws_iam_role.eb_ec2_role.name"
}

# Validate aws_eb_app
is_valid_eb_app {
        some i
    resource := input.configuration.root_module.resources[i]
    resource.type == "aws_elastic_beanstalk_application"
    resource.expressions.name
}

# Validate aws_eb_env
is_valid_eb_env {
        some i
    resource := input.configuration.root_module.resources[i]
    resource.type == "aws_elastic_beanstalk_environment"
    resource.expressions.name
    resource.expressions.application.references[0] == "aws_elastic_beanstalk_application.my_application.name"

    resource.expressions.tier.constant_value == "WebServer"
    resource.expressions.setting[0].value.references[0] == "aws_iam_instance_profile.eb_ec2_profile.name"

is_configuration_valid {
        is_valid_iam_role
    is_valid_iam_role_policy_attachment
    is_valid_iam_instance_profile
    is_valid_eb_app
    is_valid_eb_env
}

This Terraform configuration sets up a Route 53 zone named "primary" and creates two latency-based routing policies that direct traffic to the nearest endpoint based on the user's geographic location. The configuration includes:

This Terraform configuration sets up a DynamoDB table in **on-demand capacity mode**. On-demand capacity mode automatically scales to handle your workload, and you pay only for the read and write capacity you use. The configuration includes:

- A DynamoDB table with on-demand capacity mode.
- A default provisioned read and write capacity (optional, but recommended for consistency).
- A valid AWS provider configuration in the `us-east-1` region.
- No IAM roles are required for on-demand mode, as it does not require explicit capacity provisioning.

provider "aws" {

provider "aws" {

}

  name = "redshift-event-topic"

resource "aws_iam_role" "redshift_role" {
  name = "redshift-cluster-role"
  assume_role_policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Effect = "Allow"
      Principal = { Service = "redshift.amazonaws.com" }

        "redshift:DescribeClusterParameterGroups",
        "redshift:DescribeEventSubscriptions",
        "redshift:DescribeEvents",

        "redshift:DescribeClusterSecurityGroups",
        "redshift:DescribeClusterSnapshots",
        "redshift:DescribeClusterVersions",
      ]
      Resource = "*"
    }]
  })
}

  role       = aws_iam_role.redshift_role.name
  policy_arn = aws_iam_policy.redshift_policy.arn
}

  name        = "redshift-param-group"
  family      = "redshift-4.0"

**Description of the Terraform Program:**

This Terraform configuration creates an Amazon Lightsail instance with a dual-stack (IPv4 and IPv6) IP address. It uses the `hashicorp/aws` provider and sets up the necessary resources, including the Lightsail instance, and ensures that the instance is configured to support both IPv4 and IPv6. The configuration includes default values for variables such as instance name, region, and instance type, making it easy to deploy without additional input.

---

```hcl
provider "aws" {
  region = "us-east-1"
}

variable "instance_name" {
  description = "Name of the Lightsail instance"
  default     = "dualstack-lightsail-instance"
}

variable "instance_type" {
  description = "Type of the Lightsail instance"
  default     = "t2.micro"
}

variable "region" {
  description = "AWS region to deploy the Lightsail instance"
  default     = "us-east-1"
}

resource "aws_lightsail_instance" "dualstack_instance" {
  instance_name = var.instance_name
  instance_type = var.instance_type
  region        = var.region

  # Enable dual-stack (IPv4 and IPv6) support
  ipv6        = true
  public_ports = ["80", "443"]
}
```

---

- This configuration uses the `aws_lightsail_instance` resource to create a Lightsail instance.
- The `ipv6 = true` parameter enables dual-stack support.
- The `public_ports` parameter allows traffic on ports 80 and 443, which are commonly used for web services.
- The provider is configured with a default region (`us-east-1`), and all variables have default values for ease of use.
